title: Descending a local algebra essentially of finite presentation and a finitely presented module to the stages of a directed system of local rings
statement:
Let $(\Lambda,\le)$ be a nonempty directed set. Let $(A_\lambda,\mathfrak m_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ be local rings with local homomorphisms $a_{\mu\lambda}:A_\lambda	o A_\mu$ for $\lambda\le\mu$ (a ring map $\varphi:(C,\mathfrak m_C)	o(D,\mathfrak m_D)$ of local rings is *local* if $\varphi(\mathfrak m_C)\subseteq\mathfrak m_D$), $a_{\lambda\lambda}=\mathrm{id}$, $a_{
u\mu}a_{\mu\lambda}=a_{
u\lambda}$; let $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ be a local ring with local homomorphisms $\pi_\lambda:A_\lambda	o A$, $\pi_\mu a_{\mu\lambda}=\pi_\lambda$, such that $(A,(\pi_\lambda)_\lambda)$ is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of $(A_\lambda,a_{\mu\lambda})$ in the category of commutative rings. Let $(T,\mathfrak m_T)$ be a local ring and $	au:A	o T$ a local homomorphism such that $T$ is essentially of finite presentation over $A$: $T$ is isomorphic, as an $A$-algebra, to a localization $W^{-1}P$ of a finitely presented $A$-algebra $P$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] at a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq P$. Let $N$ be a finitely presented $T$-module: $N\cong\operatorname{coker}(T^{\oplus s}	o T^{\oplus t})$ for some $s,t\ge0$ and some $T$-linear map. Then there exist $\lambda_0\in\Lambda$ and, with $\Lambda_0=\{\lambda\in\Lambda:\lambda\ge\lambda_0\}$ (a nonempty directed set), the following data: for $\lambda\in\Lambda_0$ a local ring $T_\lambda$, a local homomorphism $	au_\lambda:A_\lambda	o T_\lambda$ and a $T_\lambda$-module $N_\lambda$; for $\lambda\le\mu$ in $\Lambda_0$ local homomorphisms $t_{\mu\lambda}:T_\lambda	o T_\mu$ with $t_{\mu\lambda}	au_\lambda=	au_\mu a_{\mu\lambda}$ and additive maps $n_{\mu\lambda}:N_\lambda	o N_\mu$ with $n_{\mu\lambda}(yx)=t_{\mu\lambda}(y)\,n_{\mu\lambda}(x)$ ($y\in T_\lambda$, $x\in N_\lambda$), equal to the identity for $\lambda=\mu$ and compatible with composition; for $\lambda\in\Lambda_0$ local homomorphisms $\kappa_\lambda:T_\lambda	o T$ with $\kappa_\lambda	au_\lambda=	au\pi_\lambda$ and $\kappa_\mu t_{\mu\lambda}=\kappa_\lambda$, and additive maps $
u_\lambda:N_\lambda	o N$ with $
u_\lambda(yx)=\kappa_\lambda(y)
u_\lambda(x)$ and $

u_\lambda$; such that: (1) $(T,(\kappa_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_0})$ is a colimit of $(T_\lambda,t_{\mu\lambda})_{\Lambda_0}$ in the category of commutative rings, and $(N,(
u_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_0})$ is a colimit of $(N_\lambda,n_{\mu\lambda})_{\Lambda_0}$ in the category of abelian groups; (2) every $T_\lambda$ is essentially of finite type over $A_\lambda$ via $	au_\lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]; (3) every $N_\lambda$ is the cokernel of a $T_\lambda$-linear map $T_\lambda^{\oplus s}	o T_\lambda^{\oplus t}$, in particular a finitely generated $T_\lambda$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; (4) for $\lambda\le\mu$ in $\Lambda_0$ the ring map $T_\lambda\otimes_{A_\lambda}A_\mu	o T_\mu$, $x\otimes y\mapsto t_{\mu\lambda}(x)	au_\mu(y)$, is a localization of $T_\lambda\otimes_{A_\lambda}A_\mu$ at some multiplicative subset (a ring map $C	o D$ is a *localization of $C$ at* a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq C$ if every element of $W$ maps to a unit of $D$, every element of $D$ is the image of $c$ times the inverse of the image of $w$ for some $c\in C$, $w\in W$, and $c\mapsto0$ implies $wc=0$ for some $w\in W$), and the map $N_\lambda\otimes_{T_\lambda}T_\mu	o N_\mu$, $x\otimes y\mapsto y\,n_{\mu\lambda}(x)$, is an isomorphism of $T_\mu$-modules; (5) for $\lambda\in\Lambda_0$ the ring map $T_\lambda\otimes_{A_\lambda}A	o T$, $x\otimes y\mapsto\kappa_\lambda(x)	au(y)$ ($A$ an $A_\lambda$-algebra via $\pi_\lambda$), is a localization of $T_\lambda\otimes_{A_\lambda}A$ at some multiplicative subset, and $N_\lambda\otimes_{T_\lambda}T	o N$, $x\otimes y\mapsto y\,
u_\lambda(x)$, is an isomorphism of $T$-modules.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QX (lemma-limit-module-essentially-finite-presentation, line 32427) and its proof ('We leave it to the reader to see that this works'), with the construction of the proof of Lemma Tag 00QV (lemma-limit-essentially-finite-presentation, line 32346): $T\cong(A[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m))_{\mathfrak q}$, $f_j$ descended to $A_{\lambda}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $T_\lambda=(A_\lambda[x]/(f_{1,\lambda},\dots,f_{m,\lambda}))_{\mathfrak q_\lambda}$ with $\mathfrak q_\lambda$ the inverse image of $\mathfrak q$, and $N_\lambda=\operatorname{Coker}(A_\lambda\text{-matrix})$ for a matrix descending the presentation matrix of $N$. Here the system $(A_\lambda)$ is given, not constructed, which is the form in which the proof of Lemma Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre, line 32992) uses the construction twice (for $R\to S$ over the $R_\lambda$, and for $S\to S'$ with $M$ over the $S_\lambda$). Clause (4) asks a localization at some multiplicative subset (00QX (5): at a prime ideal); clause (5) is the essentially-of-finite-presentation form of the 'in particular $M=M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S$' of Lemma Tag 00R1 (lemma-limit-module-finite-presentation, line 32593).

proof.text: Write $T\cong B_{\mathfrak q}$, with $B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ and $\mathfrak q$ the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $T$ in $B$. Indeed the given localization of a finitely presented algebra is local; every element outside that inverse image already becomes a unit, so localization once more at this prime changes nothing. The local map $A\to T$ gives $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak m_A$. The finitely many coefficients of the $f_j$ have representatives in a common $A_{\lambda_1}$; let $f_{j,\lambda}$ be their images for $\lambda\ge\lambda_1$, put $B_\lambda=A_\lambda[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_{1,\lambda},\ldots,f_{m,\lambda})$, and let $\mathfrak q_\lambda$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak q$ under $B_\lambda\to B$. Since $A_\lambda\to A$ is local and $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak m_A$, the contraction of $\mathfrak q_\lambda$ to $A_\lambda$ is its maximal ideal. Thus $T_\lambda=(B_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q_\lambda}$ is a local $A_\lambda$-algebra, essentially of finite type, and the induced maps to later stages and to $T$ are local.

source.place: Proof of Lemma Tag 00QV (lemma-limit-essentially-finite-presentation), construction of the $f_{j,\lambda}$ and $\mathfrak q_\lambda$; Lemma Tag 00QX, first paragraph of proof

proof.text: Polynomial scalar extension and quotient base change identify $B_\lambda\otimes_{A_\lambda}A_\mu$ with $B_\mu$, and $B_\lambda\otimes_{A_\lambda}A$ with $B$. Hence $B$ is the directed colimit of the $B_\lambda$: every polynomial has finitely many coefficients and comes from one stage. If a polynomial class from a stage vanishes in $B$, write its image in $A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ as a finite sum $\sum_j h_jf_j$; move the finitely many coefficients of the $h_j$ to a common later stage, then move once more so each coefficient equality in this polynomial identity holds there. The class vanishes at that stage. These two elementwise conditions make $B$ the colimit of the $B_\lambda$ in abelian groups by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-criterion] with scalar ring $\mathbb Z$; for a cocone of commutative rings the induced additive map from $B$ sends $1$ to $1$ and is multiplicative, since any two elements of $B$ come from one stage, so $B$ is the colimit in commutative rings. Applying the filtered-colimit theorem for localization at a prime to the compatible primes $\mathfrak q_\lambda$ yields $T=\varinjlim T_\lambda$; the tail above $\lambda_1$ is cofinal because the index set is directed.

source.place: Proof of Lemma Tag 00QV, final sentence ('We leave it to the reader to see that this works'); Lemma Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit)

proof.text: For $\lambda\le\mu$, base change of the localization $B_\lambda\to(B_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q_\lambda}$ identifies $T_\lambda\otimes_{A_\lambda}A_\mu$ with the localization of $B_\mu$ at the image of $B_\lambda\setminus\mathfrak q_\lambda$. That image misses $\mathfrak q_\mu$ by the definition of the inverse-image prime. Localizing this intermediate ring at the image of $B_\mu\setminus\mathfrak q_\mu$ gives $(B_\mu)_{\mathfrak q_\mu}=T_\mu$, so its canonical map to $T_\mu$ is a localization. The identical argument with $A$ in place of $A_\mu$ gives the required localization $T_\lambda\otimes_{A_\lambda}A\to T$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00QV, clause (4) and omitted final verification; Lemma Tag 00QX, clause (5)

proof.text: Choose the given presentation $T^{\oplus s}\xrightarrow{H}T^{\oplus t}\to N\to0$. Each of the finitely many entries of its $t\times s$ matrix $H$ comes from some $T_\lambda$, since $T$ is their directed colimit. Move to one common stage $\lambda_0\ge\lambda_1$ and choose a matrix $H_{\lambda_0}$ mapping to $H$; let $H_\lambda$ be its image and $N_\lambda=\operatorname{coker}(T_\lambda^{\oplus s}\xrightarrow{H_\lambda}T_\lambda^{\oplus t})$ for $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$. The maps of presentations induce compatible semilinear maps $n_{\mu\lambda}$ and $\nu_\lambda$, and the presentation shows that every $N_\lambda$ is finitely generated.

source.place: Proof of Lemma Tag 00QX, presentation matrix $A_{\lambda_2}$ and definition of $M_\lambda$

proof.text: Tensor the presentation of $N_\lambda$ with $T_\mu$ over $T_\lambda$. Tensor is right exact, and the resulting map between free $T_\mu$-modules has matrix $H_\mu$ entry by entry. Its cokernel is therefore $N_\mu$, and the induced map $N_\lambda\otimes_{T_\lambda}T_\mu\to N_\mu$ is an isomorphism. Replacing $T_\mu$ by $T$ gives $N_\lambda\otimes_{T_\lambda}T\cong N$, because the matrix then is $H$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma Tag 00QX, omitted verification after the definition of $M_\lambda$; Lemma Tag 00R1, conclusion $M=M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S$

proof.text: Finally the compatible modules $N_\lambda$ have colimit $N$ as abelian groups. Every element of $N$ is represented by a finite vector of elements of $T$, hence by a vector at one common stage, so it comes from some $N_\lambda$. If a vector class from $N_\lambda$ maps to zero in $N$, its vector in $T^{\oplus t}$ is a linear combination of the finitely many columns of $H$; move the finitely many coefficients of that combination to one later stage. Each coordinate equality then holds at a further stage by the zero criterion for the directed colimit $T=\varinjlim T_\lambda$, so the class already vanishes in some later $N_\mu$. These two elementwise conditions give the colimit universal property in abelian groups by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-criterion] applied with the fixed scalar ring $\mathbb Z$ (every $N_\lambda$, $N$, and additive transition map is canonically a $\mathbb Z$-module/map); all the claimed compatibility follows from the presentations.
